headline: Apple poaches longtime Meta executive to lead global litigation
summary: Apple has hired Scott Tucker, who served as Meta's vice president and deputy general counsel for global litigation for nearly six years.
details: Apple has officially brought on Scott Tucker, a seasoned legal executive from Meta. Tucker spent almost six years as Meta's vice president and deputy general counsel, overseeing global litigation for the social media giant.

The move, reported by Bloomberg, signifies a strategic acquisition for Apple's legal team. Tucker's extensive experience in high-stakes global litigation will be crucial as Apple navigates an increasingly complex regulatory and competitive landscape.

headline_marked: [[Replit drops Anthropic]] for OpenAI, citing cost and performance
headline: Replit drops Anthropic for OpenAI, citing cost and performance
summary: Replit CEO Amjad Masad announced the AI coding platform is no longer partnering with Anthropic, preferring OpenAI due to better performance and cost efficiency.
details: Replit CEO Amjad Masad announced the AI coding platform has ended its partnership with Anthropic. The decision was driven by multiple factors, including cost, partnership, and performance. Replit had previously announced a partnership with OpenAI in August.

Masad stated that OpenAI's ChatGPT models now perform better, according to Replit's internal benchmarks. He specifically mentioned Sol and Astra's superior performance in building vibe-coded applications from scratch. This led to the company feeling OpenAI was a better partner.

However, insiders familiar with the partnership dispute Masad's comments, claiming the collaboration between Anthropic and Replit is still active. Evidence from Replit's own website and social media posts from recent weeks shows continued use of Anthropic's Claude models. TechCrunch has reached out to Replit for clarification.

Replit, which provides a cloud-based software development platform, previously used Anthropic's Claude models to power its services. This partnership was reportedly instrumental in significantly boosting the company's revenue. The platform allows users to develop and deploy apps directly from their browser.

Masad also shared insights into Replit's business growth, noting a significant increase in enterprise revenue. Enterprise contracts now account for about 15% of revenue this year, up from 2% last year, with over 50% of total revenue coming from B2B.

He also emphasized the importance of robust AI safety measures. Masad likened the need for a "habitat" for AI agents to humans needing a conducive work environment, stressing good orchestration, error recovery, safety, security, and sandboxing.
